proposal: The Mandate notes that NAEP and other data collections release results by race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status, English proficiency, disability and sex but not by family structure, and says NAEP already collects family-structure data without releasing it. It recommends that the Department, or whichever agency collects the data long term, make student data available by family structure to the public, including in the Data Explorer tool (p. 338).

status_summary: No Department, NCES or National Assessment Governing Board action releasing or adopting reporting of NAEP results by family structure was found. A news report of 2026-08-05 states that NAEP has collected family-structure information since 2013 and has never reported it publicly, describing a July 2026 think-tank report urging release. The NAEP Data Explorer help page lists reporting groups such as gender, race and ethnicity, school lunch eligibility and English learner status and does not name a family-structure variable.
title: Publish NAEP and other federal education data by family structure
uncertainties: Searches run: two web searches by the researcher (NAEP, family structure, Data Explorer, Governing Board, NCES, 2025 and 2026) and one by the reviewer (NAEP results by family structure, Governing Board, 2026 NCES release); results were think-tank reports, news and commentary, and none reported a Department or Governing Board decision. The Data Explorer help page may not reflect the current variable list. Staffing and contract changes at the Institute of Education Sciences in 2025 were not researched because no primary or major-news source was opened. Absence of evidence rests on a limited search.
